discussion_comments.comment_body:
Acknowledged but **deferred** as a follow-up. Today no module.yaml in the tree uses `confirm` (boolean) prompts, and TEA's `true`/`false` choices are string values inside a `single-select` (so the schema yields strings, not booleans). The latent risk is real — if a future module adds a boolean `confirm` prompt, `--set foo.bar=true` would persist as the string `"true"`.

Two reasonable fixes:
1. Coerce the `--set` value at parse time based on the prompt's declared type
2. Wire `--set` through the same answer-cleaning pass used for prompted/existing answers (the path Augment suggested)

Either is more invasive than the rest of this PR's review fixes and not biting in practice today, so I'd rather track it separately than expand this PR. Will file a follow-up issue once this lands.

Resolved in f1c9e12. Good catch — this was the most important fix. Took a slightly different path than the suggested one in your prompt:

Instead of widening `overrideKeys` inside `partition()` to also include any undeclared keys from `moduleConfigs`, I made `collectModuleConfig` carry forward the keys from `_existingConfig[moduleName]` into `collectedConfig[moduleName]` AND track them in `setOverrideKeys`. That way `partition()`'s contract stays tight ("keep keys explicitly asserted as overrides") instead of becoming "keep any key that happens to be in cfg", which would weaken the schema-strict filter against legacy spread-from-core pollution.

End-to-end verified:

```
$ bmad install --yes --modules bmm --set bmm.future_thing=hello   # run #1
▲ --set bmm.future_thing — 'future_thing' is not a declared config key for module 'bmm'; persisted but unused by current install.
$ grep future_thing _bmad/config.toml
future_thing = "hello"

$ bmad install --yes --action update --modules bmm                # run #2, NO --set
$ grep future_thing _bmad/config.toml
future_thing = "hello"   # ← survives
```

Test coverage added in suite 44 (carry-forward case).

Fixed in b768e0b3 — added the same `alreadyDecided` guard at the top of the stable branch (`channelOptions.global || nextSet.has(code) || pins.has(code)`). Explicit `--pin`/`--next=`/`--channel` overrides now skip upgrade classification entirely instead of being overwritten by `prev.version` on decline/major-refuse/fetch-error.
And you should probably use this.bmadFolderName instead of hardcoded _bmad in template paths
